concept: Refraction of Light Through a Glass Slab

artifact.topic: Refraction of Light Through a Glass Slab

cards.title: The bending straw
cards.idea: A straw in a glass of water looks broken at the surface. Light from the straw bends as it leaves water into air, fooling your eye.

interaction.prompt: Tap the spot where the straw looks broken

cards.reveal: The break sits exactly at the water surface, where light crosses from one medium into another and changes direction.

cards.title: Bending at the boundary
cards.idea: A ray hits a glass slab at an angle. Slide the incoming angle and watch how the ray bends as it enters and exits.

interaction.prompt: Slide the angle of incidence from 0 to 60 degrees

cards.reveal: Entering glass, the ray bends toward the normal (denser medium). Leaving glass, it bends away. Bigger incidence, bigger bend.

cards.title: In and out
cards.idea: Trace the ray through the slab: air, glass, air. Compare the direction it entered with the direction it left.

interaction.prompt: Drag the arrow to show the direction of the ray after it leaves the slab

cards.reveal: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray. It is only shifted sideways, not turned. This shift is called lateral displacement.

cards.title: Naming the rule
cards.idea: Denser medium bends light toward the normal; rarer medium bends it away. A parallel-sided slab shifts the ray sideways but keeps its final direction unchanged.

interaction.prompt: Tap the term that means the sideways shift

cards.reveal: Lateral displacement. It grows with a thicker slab and a larger angle of incidence, and it is zero when light enters straight along the normal.

cards.title: Straight through
cards.idea: Send a ray straight into the slab, along the normal, at 90 degrees to the surface.

interaction.prompt: Tap the ray that passes without bending

cards.reveal: At zero angle of incidence the ray goes straight through, no bending, no shift. Refraction needs the ray to strike at an angle.

cards.title: Which way it bends
cards.idea: Air to glass, then glass to air. Match each crossing to whether the ray bends toward or away from the normal.

interaction.prompt: Drag each label to the correct crossing

cards.reveal: Air to glass: toward the normal. Glass to air: away from the normal. Entering denser slows and bends toward; leaving denser speeds and bends away.

workbook.prompt: When light passes from air into a glass slab, it bends
The sideways shift between the incident ray and the emergent ray from a slab is called ________.
How does the emergent ray compare with the incident ray for a parallel glass slab
options: it is parallel to the incident ray
it is perpendicular to the incident ray
workbook.answer: it is parallel to the incident ray

boss.prompt: A ray hits a glass slab along the normal (angle of incidence zero). What happens
options: it passes straight through without bending
it bends away from the normal
it reflects back to the source
boss.answer: it passes straight through without bending

boss.prompt: To increase the lateral displacement of a ray through a slab, you can use a ________ slab.
Why does a ray bend away from the normal as it leaves the glass and re-enters air
options: it moves into a rarer, faster medium
it moves into a denser, slower medium
it stops changing speed at the boundary
boss.answer: it moves into a rarer, faster medium
